page: Amazon Web Services c7a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized Seventh Generation instance powered by the AWS Nitro Hypervisor. It features 96 physical AMD EPYC 9R14 cores operating at 3.7 GHz with dedicated allocation and a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio. The x86_64 architecture incorporates advanced instruction set extensions including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, VAES, and SHA_NI. System memory consists of 192.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 RAM running at 5 GHz, delivering a memory density of 2.0 GB per physical core.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 38 Gbps and operates without bundled local NVMe storage. Benchmark measurements place multi-core throughput in the top tier across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests, alongside high-tier results in software compilation with Clang and PassMark CPU physics processing. Cached memory read throughput reaches 12,128.93 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads achieve 348.43 GB/sec. The instance also demonstrates high performance in key-value data stores, achieving 172.4 million Redis SET operations per second.

By pairing 96 dedicated physical cores with DDR5 memory, c7a.24xlarge optimizes compute-dense execution efficiency by eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The 2 GB per core ratio represents a functional tradeoff, prioritizing raw processing power and instruction throughput over large memory footprints. Lacking bundled local ephemeral storage, it relies on network-attached block storage for state persistence. This hardware profile aligns with compute-heavy workloads such as parallel software compilation, CPU-based LLM inference, scientific simulation, and high-throughput web serving.
